# Core-conformance census — the UI tier

<!-- GENERATED by src/Fuaran.UI.Tests/CoreConformanceCensus.fs. Do not hand-edit: the
     suite regenerates this file and fails when the committed copy has drifted. -->

Every public law family the pinned `Fuaran.Core.Conformance` **0.36.0** and `Fuaran.Compute.Conformance` **0.38.1** ship, and how this repo answers for it.

A family with no row fails the suite, and so does a row naming a family the pinned kit no
longer ships — enrolment is by name AND by reflection, and the two are checked against
each other. `Carried by phase` is an enrolment a named roadmap phase will flip to
`Adopted` when it ships.

`Cases` is what the run that regenerated this file measured: the subject laws an adopting
test's run reported, times the iterations it was driven over. `vacuous (<dimension>)` names
a side of the family the sample never reached (the adequacy guard went red for it) rather
than a defect — `Conformance.containerLaws` reads this way by design, per the test that
adopts it. `—` marks a row nothing in THIS test project's process ran: `NotUsed` /
`SiblingHost` / `CarriedBy` rows, and — today — every `Adopted` row whose test lives in one
of this repo's OTHER test projects (`Fuaran.UI.OpStream.Tests`, `.OpStream.Dag.Tests`,
`.ServerDriven.Tests`, `.FastPath.Tests`), which this run never executes and so cannot
count without inventing a figure. Measuring those is a named follow-on, not a silent gap:
see the `measuredHere` set in `CoreConformanceCensus.fs`.
